Currently selected: Smarter choices for developers Smarter choices for developers More control for administrators Billing Get started GitHub Copilot Fusion is generally available. Instead of picking a model for each task, choose Copilot Fusion and let Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate which models it uses for you. Copilot Fusion brings together Project HydraFusion’s multi-model orchestration and Copilot auto model selection’s fine-tuned model selection, leveraging the benefits of both to balance performance and cost efficiency. Since Project HydraFusion launched, we’ve improved its performance. In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Copilot Fusion Max scored 60, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max. It delivered that result at about half the average API cost per task, using about half as many tokens and taking about 40% less time per task. Smarter choices for developers When you select Copilot Fusion in the model picker, you aren’t selecting a specific model. You’re choosing a system that routes and orchestrates models for each task. There’s no need to switch models during a task or decide which model suits each step. For each prompt, Copilot Fusion determines which models to use and how they work together, while you choose the right level of effort. To use it, select Copilot Fusion in the model picker, then choose the effort level. Fusion Standard: Prioritizes versatile models for everyday coding. title: Generate and edit images directly in Copilot - GitHub Changelog
excerpt: You can now generate and edit images using natural language in GitHub Copilot. When you ask for an image, your selected reasoning model calls a dedicated image-generation tool powered by…
body_excerpt: Generate and edit images directly in Copilot - GitHub Changelog Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app See what's new Search Changelog Docs Customer stories See what's new Try GitHub Copilot app Back to changelog Release October 28, 2026 • 1 minute read Generate and edit images directly in Copilot You can now generate and edit images using natural language in GitHub Copilot. When you ask for an image, your selected reasoning model calls a dedicated image-generation tool powered by GPT Image 2.5 Flare, previews the result inline, and saves it to your project. Previously, getting a visual asset while working in Copilot meant stepping away to a separate tool, describing what you needed again, generating it there, and manually bringing it back into your project. This update removes that context switch, so you can go from an idea to a usable image without breaking your flow. Describe an image conversationally in any Copilot chat session, whether you’re starting a new request or in the middle of a coding task. Copilot previews the generated image inline and saves it directly to your workspace. Organization and enterprise owners can turn off image generation by disabling the image generation model using Copilot model policies . You can opt in to a visible “Made with AI” watermark on images Copilot generates and edits. Watermarking is off by default. To try it, open a Copilot chat in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, or Copilot CLI and describe the image you want. Image generation is in public preview for Copilot Pro, Copilot Pro+, Copilot Business, and Copilot Enterprise. It’s billed separately from your chat model, based on image tokens that count toward your plan’s AI credits. Currently selected: Managed download and setup on Windows Managed download and setup on Windows Bring your own local model Today we are shipping intelligent routing for local models into experimental preview. GitHub Copilot Fusion can now choose between supported on-device models and cloud models, enabling intelligent local model routing in GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot app, and Visual Studio Code. This opt-in experimental preview lets you use your device’s compute without switching models manually for each request. For a deeper dive into this feature, see our original announcement on October 7th . Managed download and setup on Windows On supported Windows devices, you can download and configure MAI Code 1.1 Flash through the Windows ML provider. In Copilot CLI , enable experimental mode and open /model to follow the setup prompts. In the Copilot app , configure the Windows ML provider under Settings > Model providers , enable Local model auto routing under Settings > Experiments , and start a new session. Windows ML local models is enabled by default on Windows. In VS Code , enable chat.copilot.localModel.enabled . Once the model is ready, select Standard in Copilot Fusion to let Copilot choose between local and cloud models. You can also select the local model directly for your session. Bring your own local model The managed download experience is Windows-only, but Copilot CLI’s local Copilot Fusion routing also works with manually configured models on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
